claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in South Karelia wellbeing services county was 4.0% below the national level (ratio 0.96, 95% interval 0.92-1), about 14.7 fewer deaths a year than its age structure predicts.
No measured pathway stage shows South Karelia wellbeing services county clearly worse than the country; if outcomes differ, the cause is not locatable from public data.

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 6 deaths a year in South Karelia wellbeing services county (range 0.9-12) for an assumed EUR 186,357 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 89% of sensitivity runs.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 74.1% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 51% of the gap.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 75.7% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-4.27 percentage points, closing about 70% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
